title: Trump Refers Habba's Claim of a Missing Kennedy Center Donation Under Grenell to White House Counsel
institution: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts; White House Counsel's Office
status: Under White House counsel and Kennedy Center review; allegation unproven and denied
what_changed: Alina Habba, President Trump's former personal attorney, told Trump in the Oval Office that Ric Grenell, who ran the Kennedy Center from February 2025 until March 2026, **failed to deposit a multimillion-dollar donation her husband, Turkish businessman Turhan Mildon, made to the center about a year earlier.** Axios, citing four senior administration officials and three other people briefed on the dispute, reported on Oct. 14, 2026 that Trump referred the allegation to White House Counsel Will Scharf to look into. According to Habba's account, Grenell persuaded Mildon in the spring of 2025 to fold the donation into a $17.6 million wire transfer for a business deal involving a U.S. company. Habba first put the donation at $17 million, then at $5.6 million; Axios's sources also described it as nearly $6 million. Grenell called the claim "absurd" and a lie, saying "I've never received any payment from him at all." A senior administration official said the claims were only allegations. When Axios reported, counsel had asked for documentation but received none; the New York Times later reported that Mildon's lawyer sent Scharf text messages and a wire transfer receipt that night. Grenell denies sending a text attributed to him, and no outlet has verified the documents. Kennedy Center staff who searched for the donation in late 2025 could not find it; the only record they found showed Mildon owed a $270,000 pledge, which he paid on Oct. 13, 2026, after the New York Times asked about it. The center says it is reviewing relevant pledges and funds. The dispute reportedly grew out of Grenell and Mildon's shared interests in Venezuela.

primary_proponent.name: Ric Grenell
primary_proponent.role: Former president of the Kennedy Center (February 2025 to March 2026)
primary_proponent.note: Accused by Alina Habba of failing to deposit her husband's donation; he denies it and says he never received any payment from Mildon.

estimated_impact.summary: If true, a donation of several million dollars intended for the Kennedy Center never reached it; if false, the claim is a dispute among Trump allies now before the White House counsel.

estimated_impact.caveat: Every dollar figure here comes from Habba's side or from anonymous officials; no audit, filing or official finding confirms any money went missing, and the center's own search found only a $270,000 pledge.

confidence_note: LOW confidence on the underlying allegation, HIGH confidence that it was made and referred. Axios broke the story from four senior administration officials and three other insiders, and the New York Times and Washington Post confirmed the Oval Office account independently, with Grenell's on-record denial. The New York Times reported that Mildon's lawyer sent Scharf text messages and a wire transfer receipt on Oct. 14; Grenell disputes at least one of the texts, and no outlet has verified the documents. Frame it as an unproven accusation under internal review, not as a finding of missing money.

section_summaries.what_changed: Trump sent Alina Habba's claim that Ric Grenell never deposited her husband's multimillion-dollar Kennedy Center donation to his White House counsel.
section_summaries.estimated_impact: Millions meant for the Kennedy Center may be unaccounted for, but the only record the center found is a $270,000 pledge, paid Oct. 13, 2026.
section_summaries.confidence_note: The allegation and referral are well reported; the missing money itself is unproven, unverified and denied by Grenell.
